courses.title: Introductory Course of Machinery Vibration (Category I prep)
courses.summary: Basic machinery vibration monitoring and diagnostic activities; recommended as partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category I Certification Exam.
courses.overview: This course prepares candidates to perform basic machinery vibration monitoring and diagnostic activities. It is recommended for partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category I Certification Exam.
topics: Vibration sources and effects; characteristics, measurement conventions, properties, and units
Vectors and their significance in vibration measurements; rotational speed; vibration measures and conversions
Choosing the right measurement for the application
Digital signal-processing basics; analog and digital signals
Sensor types, features, characteristics, power-supply requirements, mounting methods, and limitations
Time and frequency domains; FFT basics and limitations
Data-collection parameters: frequency span, samples, resolution, sampling frequency, Nyquist theorem, aliasing, windowing, analog-to-digital conversion, and averaging
Forcing and natural frequencies, resonance, and critical speeds
Fault-frequency identification and common faults: unbalance, misalignment, looseness, and electrical faults
Vibration severity charts, condition evaluation, fault evaluation, standards, and acceptance testing
Workshops and demonstrations covering measurements, data collection, spectrum analysis, fault analysis, and vibration severity
receives: Workshops containing examples and workshop problems

courses.title: Intermediate Course on Machinery Vibration Analysis Level III
courses.summary: In-depth single-channel time waveform, FFT and phase analysis for evaluating industrial machinery, with partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category III Certification Exam.
courses.overview: This course provides more in-depth discussions of single-channel time waveform, FFT, and phase analysis techniques for the evaluation of industrial machinery. It includes acceptance testing, machine severity assessment, use of demodulation and HFE techniques, basic rotor dynamics, basic ODS, and single-plane balancing. This course is partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category III Certification Exam. Workshops and demonstrations scheduled throughout the training course illustrate theory and applications.
topics: Time and frequency analysis: time-domain and FFT displays and analysis, modulation, clipping, pulsation, beats, side bands, spectrum shape, synchronous and nonsynchronous signals, and case histories
Phase and orbit analysis: phase measurement and analysis, orbit evaluation, loop rules, and case histories

Machinery vibration analysis techniques, resonance and critical-speed testing: interference diagrams, analyzer setup for impact and transient tests, test procedures, Bode/polar plot evaluation, and case histories
Machine condition evaluation: criteria, levels, maintenance actions, standards, overall-band, spectral, orbital and time-waveform evaluation, and alarm setting
Basic vibration control: isolation, damping, resonance elimination, concepts, hardware, foundations, and pedestals
Field balancing techniques: single-plane balancing, trial-weight size and location, balance sensitivity, and phase lag
Balancing exercises: measure selection, frequency spans, and time, frequency, and orbital displays
Transducers: proximity probes, accelerometers, optical pickups, selection, location, and mounting
Data acquisition and basic data-collector setup: sampling, triggering, window selection, resolution, dynamic range, and averaging
Basic analysis techniques: orders and direct-frequency spectrum analysis, including side bands
Analysis of operating-speed faults: orders, mass unbalance, misalignment, looseness, distortion, rubs, resonance, bearing wear, and case histories
Gear and bearing analysis: measurement methods, frequencies, analysis techniques, and case histories
Motors, fans, and pumps: basics, frequencies, techniques, and analysis
Fault analysis and machine-condition evaluation: measures, procedures, severity charts, and alarm settings
Machine testing: test plans, impact testing, and acceptance testing
Periodic monitoring: screening, alarm setup, measurement frequency, trending, and reports
Fundamentals of single-plane balancing
Machine analysis, course review, a one-and-a-half-hour examination on course content, and examination review
receives: Workshops containing examples and workshop problems

courses.title: Dynamic Balancing of Rotors
courses.summary: An introduction to the balancing process, balancing-machine design, instrumentation, tooling, unbalance measurement and correction, with demonstrations and hands-on exercises.
courses.overview: This course provides a basic understanding of the balancing process. Participants learn the design principles of different balancing machines, how to use instrumentation and different tooling applications, balancing theory, types of imbalance, methods of correction, and measurements of unbalance. Demonstrations and hands-on exercises provide an opportunity to practise the skills covered.
topics: Different types of unbalance: static, couple, and dynamic
ISO tolerance and terminology
Design principles of hard- and soft-bearing balancing machines
Theory of unbalance measurement and correction
Principles of tool design and avoiding tooling errors
Unbalance versus centrifugal-force determination
Correlation of unbalance and displacement of centre of gravity
Causes of unbalance errors
Rigid and flexible rotors
Selecting proper unbalance tolerance and balancing speed
Plane separation
Introduction to flexible rotors
Balancing-machine testing
Introduction to field balancing

courses.title: Machinery Vibration Fundamentals Level II
courses.summary: Basic machinery vibration analysis using single-channel measurements, with partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category II Certification Exam.
courses.overview: This course prepares attendees to perform basic machinery vibration analysis on industrial machinery using single-channel measurements, with or without trigger signals, according to established procedures. It covers sensors, database and data-collector setup, data collection, signal processing, fault analysis, and the basics of single-plane balancing. It is partial preparation for the Vibration Analyst Category II Certification Exam. Workshops and demonstrations illustrate theory and applications.
topics: Vibration sources and effects; characteristics, measurement conventions, properties, and units
Vectors, rotational speed, vibration measures and conversions, and selecting measures
Digital signal-processing basics; analog and digital signals; sensors and mounting
Time and frequency domains, FFT, data collection, triggering, sampling, aliasing, windowing, averaging, and dynamic range
Single-mass oscillating systems with and without damping
Fault-frequency identification and relation of operating speed to faults
Motors, pumps, and compressors; unbalance, misalignment, looseness, resonance, critical speed, distortion, and bearing wear
Beats and modulation; gearbox and bearing measurement and analysis
Impact testing, run-up/coast-down, severity assessment, alarm limits, condition evaluation, acceptance testing, and report generation
Transducers, proximity probes, accelerometers, optical pickups, selection, location, and mounting
Data-collector setup, direct-frequency spectrum analysis, operating-speed faults, and case histories
Gear and bearing analysis; motors, fans, pumps, and machine testing
Periodic monitoring, trending, reports, and fundamentals of single-plane balancing
receives: Workshops containing examples and workshop problems

courses.title: Vibration Analysis and Rotor Balancing Course
courses.summary: Vibration data collection, time waveform, spectral and phase analysis, fault-frequency interpretation, and the basics of single-plane rotor balancing.
courses.overview: This course provides a more in-depth understanding of basic vibration data collection, parameter setup, time waveform, spectral and phase analysis, and the basics of single-plane rotor balancing. Identification and interpretation of fault frequencies are examined. Discussions cover single-channel and multi-channel time waveform, FFT, and phase analysis techniques for evaluating industrial machinery, single-plane in-situ balancing procedures, the mass-spring-damper system, and the importance of critical speed in balancing.
topics: Vibration data collection: measures, units, conversion, sensors, configuration, and analyzer setup for routine and off-route measurements
Time and frequency analysis: time-domain and FFT displays and analysis, modulation, clipping, pulsation, beats, side bands, spectrum shape, synchronous and nonsynchronous signals, and case histories
Phase and orbit analysis: phase measurement and analysis, orbit evaluation, loop rules, and case histories
Mass-spring-damper system: response of a single-mass oscillating system to various frequencies
Rigid and flexible rotors, critical speed, Bode plot, and slow-roll vector compensation
Fundamentals of rotor balancing
Different types of unbalance: static, couple, and dynamic
ISO tolerance and terminology
Design principles of hard- and soft-bearing balancing machines
Theory of unbalance measurement and correction
Basics of in-situ or field balancing
Pre-balancing checks
Single-plane balancing exercise using the influence coefficient method

courses.title: Experimental Modal Analysis
courses.summary: Modal testing, measurement methods, frequency response functions, system response, and modal parameter extraction.
courses.overview: This course covers modal testing applications, measurement methods, and analysis processes, including single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems, frequency response functions, test planning, measurement systems, excitation methods, and modal parameter extraction.
topics: Introduction to modal testing, applications, measurement methods, and analysis processes
Terminology and notations
Single-degree-of-freedom system theory
Presentation and properties of the frequency response function (FRF)
Data for single-degree-of-freedom systems
Undamped multi-degree-of-freedom systems
Multi-degree-of-freedom systems with proportional, structural, and viscous damping
Modal analysis of rotating structures and complex modes
Characteristics and presentation of multi-degree-of-freedom FRF data
Response-function measurement techniques and test planning
Basic measurement systems, structure preparation, and excitation
Transducers, amplifiers, analysers, and digital signal processing
Excitation signals and calibration
Mass cancellation and rotational FRF measurement
Measurements on non-linear structures and multi-point excitation
Modal parameter extraction methods

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing Fundamentals
courses.summary: Fundamentals of signals and systems, sampling, transforms, filters, signal averaging, and data formats.
courses.overview: Course topics include continuous-time signals and systems, discrete sequences and systems, sampling, Fourier transforms, filters, quadrature signals, the Hilbert transform, sampling-rate conversion, signal averaging, digital data formats, and the Laplace transform.
topics: Introduction to signals and systems
Continuous-time signals and systems
Discrete sequences and systems
Periodic sampling
Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)
Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
Finite impulse response (FIR) filters
Infinite impulse response filters
Types of filters
Quadrature signals
Discrete Hilbert Transform
Sampling-rate conversion
Signal averaging
Digital data formats and effects
Laplace Transform

courses.title: Online and Offline Vibration Measurement Systems
courses.summary: Online and offline measurement systems, instrumentation, vibration analysis plots, transient and steady-state data collection, and rotor-bearing systems.
courses.overview: Course topics cover the differences between online and offline vibration measurement, choosing a system, sensors and instrumentation, data collection and processing limitations, vibration plots, steady-state and transient data collection, and rotor-bearing system behavior.
topics: Differences between online and offline vibration measurement
Choosing the right system
Sensor types and applications
Instrumentation for data collection and analysis
Limitations of data collection and processing
Vibration plots: time base, spectra, full spectra, orbit, shaft centreline, trend, Bode, Nyquist, and polar
Time-domain, frequency-domain, and phase analysis
Steady-state and transient data-collection techniques
Rotor-bearing systems
Resonance and critical speeds
Lubrication and its influence
Instability of rotor-bearing systems
Stiffness, damping, and their influence
Unbalance and balancing procedure
ISO guidelines
API guidelines

courses.title: Advanced Vibration Analysis Training
courses.summary: Hands-on training covering vibration analysis, data acquisition, fault diagnostics, and rigid and flexible rotor balancing.
courses.overview: Hands-on advanced vibration analysis training using Rotor Kit RK4, PT400 Mini, and DAQ systems ADRE 208 and TWave T8.
topics: Basics
DAQ configuration
Vibration data collection
Signal processing
Balancing rigid and flexible rotors
Oil whirl and rubs
Gearbox and bearing fault simulation and detection
Rolling element bearing fault analysis
Resonance and critical-speed testing

Corrective action and reporting
Operational Deflection Shape (ODS) analysis
Natural frequency identification using an instrumented impact hammer

courses.summary: Online course covering vibration fundamentals, data acquisition, signal processing, diagnostics, rotor balancing and vibration plots.
courses.overview: The supplied online-course poster lists topics covering vibration fundamentals, data acquisition, signal processing, fault diagnostics, balancing, plots, resonance, operating deflection shapes, standards, and corrective-action reporting.
